newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia sorghum market remains subdued-Grainco.
newsitem.headline: Australia sorghum market remains subdued-Grainco.

text.p: The southern Queensland sorghum market remains subdued with relatively limited traded over the past week, Queensland co-operative Grainco Ltd said in its weekly market report.
Growers and consumers alike continue to watch the weather, progress of the winter plant and wheat values for price direction.
With the new financial year approaching, the next three to four weeks would either see renewed grower selling or continuing reluctance if dry weather remains a concern, Grainco said.
In central Queensland, values finished the week a litte lower around A$120 per tonne delivered port, with little fresh news to report either domestically or internationally.
Export market continues to watch the progress of the U.S. corn crop for any problems which may result in a short-term kick in the futures.

With the barley harvest in Southern Europe commencing in about two weeks the international market would be closely watching to see the actual harvest yields in these early crops for near term price direction, Grainco said.

Supportive news came from the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics' (ABARE) recent reduction in Australia's barley production to 5.8 mmt given the forecasted El Nino weather pattern.
Further rainfall was needed in eastern Australia to complete barley planting.
In Queensland, falls of 25-50 mm were needed across the southern and central downs in the next three to four weeks to achieve the current planting estimates of 150,000 hectares.

Domestic old crop feed barley values finished the week unchanged at A$175/mt delivered Brisbane for June/July, reflecting a premium over export values which have remained steady at around US$140/mt on an fob basis.
New crop values finished the week at A$153/mt delivered Brisbane for the November-December delivery period.
Domestic new corp malting barley values remained supported in the international market and by domestic weather influences at around A$183/mt delivered port.

Continuing strong export demand for cotton from the Japanese and Korean markets was being seen for prompt shipment right through until new crop, however export price ideas were still well below levels being six to eight weeks ago.
Despite there being two cargoes of seed committed for bulk export, traditional container consumers believed prices should weaken as the supply of Australian seed remains plentiful.
Mediocre domestic feed offtake, softer crushing margins and a delay in the crush uptake all tend to support this view.
However, export consumers were failing to take note of the fact that available seed was being aggregated in strong hands.
The power of the export consumer was not to be understimated as they were very good at manipulating the market to suit their requirements, Grainco said.
Australian marketers would need to maintain a strong price stance across the board in order to work prices higher.
Cash prices continued to trade around A$145 per tonne to A$150 Downs gin to the grower.
In central Queensland prices had firmed to A$150 ex gin for ginning period delivery to domestic consumers.
Sowing of pulses continues in much of Queensland and northern New South Wales where conditions allow.
In drier areas, many farmers were still intending to plant some acreage to pulses, however they were awaiting further rains.
Price indications for the new crop continue at around the A$310 to A$315 delivered port basis for Queensland chickpeas and faba beans at around A$250 port for the new crop.
Domestic values were slightly higher with sunflowers finishing the week at A$327/mt delivered Newcastle for June/July.
Central Queensland sunflower prices finished the week at A$282 - A$287 a tonne delivered central Queensland depot (depending on location) for the June - July delivery period.
New crop soybean prices moved lower at A$415 delivered Brisbane.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2-9372-1800
